title: Report a partially applied VCF 9.0 host commissioning change accurately
prompt:
Implement the `vcf_onboard` package in this repository. It drives one multi-step change against a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager appliance: create a network pool, attach an extra IP pool to one of that pool's networks, validate a set of ESXi host commission specifications, then commission those hosts. The change is not transactional, the last step fails, and the report the tool writes is the only record of what is now true on the appliance.

Standard library only, Python 3.10 or later. Write only files under `vcf_onboard/`. `docs/`, `fixtures/` and `tests/` are protected; do not modify them.

Read `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The contract was derived from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. Rendered documentation pages are not a source, and neither is the 9.1.0.0 revision of the same file, which differs. Use exactly these operationIds and no others: `createToken` (`POST /v1/tokens`), `createNetworkPool` (`POST /v1/network-pools`), `addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool` (`POST /v1/network-pools/{id}/networks/{networkId}/ip-pools`), `validateHostCommissionSpec` (`POST /v1/hosts/validations`), `commissionHosts` (`POST /v1/hosts`) and `getTask` (`GET /v1/tasks/{id}`).

Command line:

```
python3 -m vcf_onboard --base-url URL --plan PATH --report PATH [--poll-interval SECONDS] [--poll-timeout SECONDS]
```

`--poll-interval` defaults to 10.0 and `--poll-timeout` to 3600.0. Credentials come from `VCF_SDDC_USERNAME` and `VCF_SDDC_PASSWORD`. Exit 0 when every step succeeded, 2 when the change ran but a step failed, and 1 for a usage or environment error. Write the report whenever at least one step was attempted.

Wire requirements:

- `application/json` for `Content-Type` and `Accept`. Every request except `createToken` carries `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` from the `TokenPair`; `createToken` is sent unauthenticated.
- An optional field with no value is omitted from the body. Never send it as null, an empty string, an empty array, an empty object, 0 or false. A network with no IP pools carries no `ipPools` key; a host with no SSH thumbprint carries no `sshThumbprint` key; `createToken` sends only `username` and `password`, never `apiKey` or `idToken`.
- Never send a server-assigned property: `NetworkPool.id`, `NetworkPool.hostsCount`, `Network.id`, `Network.freeIps`, `Network.usedIps`.
- `vlanId` and `mtu` are JSON numbers. None of these operations declares a query parameter, so no request carries a query string. `getTask` requests are bodyless.
- Take every identifier from a response. The `networkPoolId` on each host specification and the `{id}` and `{networkId}` path segments of the IP pool request come from the `createNetworkPool` response.
- The same host specification list is sent to `validateHostCommissionSpec` and then unchanged to `commissionHosts`. Validation is fatal only when its `resultStatus` is `FAILED`; a `WARNING` check does not stop the change but must be reported. The validation response is terminal on arrival, there is no validation polling operation in this contract, and there is no rollback: a step that already succeeded stays.

`fixtures/onboarding_plan.json` holds the change. `networkPool` goes to `createNetworkPool`. `additionalIpPool` names a `networkType`; attach its `start` and `end` to the network of that type in the created pool. `hosts` become `HostCommissionSpec` items with `networkPoolId` added.

`commissionHosts` returns 202 with a `Task`. Poll `getTask` on `--poll-interval` until the status is terminal: `IN_PROGRESS` and `PENDING` are not terminal, `SUCCESSFUL` is success, `FAILED` and `CANCELLED` are failure. The task's `subTasks` carry the per-host outcome; each sub-task identifies its host through `resources[0].fqdn`, and a sub-task that reached `SUCCESSFUL` carries the `resourceId` SDDC Manager assigned. A partly failed task is normal: some hosts are commissioned, one fails, the rest stay `PENDING`. Report that as it is, do not flatten it into "commissioning failed".

The report is JSON with `schemaVersion` `"vcf-onboard/report/1"`, `planName`, `sddcManager` (the `--base-url` value), `overallStatus` (`SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED`), `steps`, `hosts`, `completedChanges`, and `failure` when the run failed.

`steps` always lists all five, in order, as `{"name", "operationId", "status", "details"}` with `status` one of `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` or `NOT_ATTEMPTED`. The names are `authenticate`, `create_network_pool`, `add_ip_pool`, `validate_hosts`, `commission_hosts`. Details: `create_network_pool` carries `networkPoolId`, `networkPoolName` and `networkIds` mapping network type to assigned id; `add_ip_pool` carries `networkPoolId`, `networkId`, `start` and `end`; `validate_hosts` carries `validationId`, `executionStatus`, `resultStatus` and `warnings` holding the descriptions of the `WARNING` checks; `commission_hosts` carries `taskId` and `taskStatus` verbatim from the task.

`hosts` holds `{"fqdn", "status"}` per host in plan order, with the sub-task status verbatim, plus `resourceId` for a commissioned host and `errorCode` and `message` for a failed one. It is empty when commissioning never ran.

`completedChanges` lists only what exists on the appliance now, in the order it was made: `{"kind": "NETWORK_POOL", "id", "name"}`, then `{"kind": "IP_POOL", "networkPoolId", "networkId", "start", "end"}`, then one `{"kind": "HOST", "fqdn", "resourceId"}` per host whose sub-task reached `SUCCESSFUL`. A step that failed or never ran contributes nothing.

`failure` is `{"step", "operationId", "message"}` plus `errorCode` and `taskId` when the appliance supplied them and `httpStatus` when the failure was an HTTP error response.

Never write a password into the report, stdout or stderr.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts a contract-pinned mock SDDC Manager on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port, runs `python3 -m vcf_onboard` against it twice, and asserts the exact request sequence, headers and body bytes from the mock's request log together with the accuracy of the report. The mock serves only the six contract operations and rejects any request the 9.0 schemas would reject. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: a network pool is created, an IP pool is attached to its vSAN network and three host commission specifications validate with one warning, then the commissioning task settles FAILED with one host commissioned, one host failed and one host never attempted
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact request wire shape including omission of every unset optional field, and the report must attribute the four steps that landed, the partial effect of the failed step and the steps that never ran
